editorial_note: Sources distinguish ICE, CBP, and DHS; attribution of agency roles matters. Dates and framing should be verified before public release.

events.fact: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is established under the new Department of Homeland Security.
ICE arrests 389 workers at the Agriprocessors plant in Postville, Iowa, in a raid that reshapes community debates about enforcement and due process.

The federal zero-tolerance policy produces widespread family separations at the southern border; DHS inspectors document failures in tracking and reunification. The policy involved multiple DHS agencies, including CBP and ICE.
ICE arrests approximately 680 workers at seven Mississippi poultry plants, one of the largest workplace enforcement actions of the period.
Large immigration enforcement operations in Los Angeles and Chicago trigger protests, legal disputes and intense debate over public safety and civil liberties.
Operation Metro Surge in Minnesota becomes a national flashpoint after broad enforcement, community protests and the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by federal officers.
